subject.title: after_tool_call hook receives a flattened string, not the structured ToolResult — plugins cannot detect exec/bash failures

question: Should OpenClaw canonicalize Codex-native shell/apply_patch after_tool_call payloads into structured OpenClaw results, and what text compatibility field should remain for existing plugins?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the repair changes a public plugin hook payload/timing boundary and must choose between native-relay immediacy, app-server structured fidelity, duplicate-event suppression, and string-result compatibility.

options.title: Structured OpenClaw payload
options.body: Use app-server commandExecution/fileChange completion data as the single plugin-visible after_tool_call result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch and suppress the duplicate raw string relay for those tools.

options.title: Add structured companion field
options.body: Keep result as the native string temporarily and add a documented structured result/details field, accepting a longer compatibility path and a slightly wider hook payload.

options.title: Leave native string contract
options.body: Document native Codex PostToolUse strings as the intended plugin contract and direct exit-code consumers to another surface, leaving this operator pain unresolved.

recommendation.title: Structured OpenClaw payload
recommendation.body: Use app-server commandExecution/fileChange completion data as the single plugin-visible after_tool_call result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch and suppress the duplicate raw string relay for those tools.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits on the plugin hook/tool-result API boundary introduced in the middleware work, with Codex app-server owners able to implement the selected payload shape.
